newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Court hears Nigerian activist held over bombings.
newsitem.headline: Court hears Nigerian activist held over bombings.

text.p: A Nigerian activist detained since December was being held over bomb explosions in Lagos, newspapers reported on Friday.
Medical doctor Frederick Fasehun, chairman of the Campaign for Democracy (CD) pressure group, was taken from his home last month after police searched his home and hospital.

The newspapers said that last week Justice Mutiu Bishogun of the Lagos high court ordered that Fasehun should be released, saying his detention was a violation of his fundamental human rights, but the State Security Service (SSS) on Thursday appealed against the order.

"The detainee was arrested in connection with the recent bomb attacks on innocent citizens in Lagos state which claimed so many lives and destroyed valuable properties," the SSS said in a counter affidavit to the court.
No date has been fixed for when its appeal will he heard.

Nigerian police have blamed the umbrella opposition group NADECO, of which CD is a member, for three bomb blasts that have shaken Lagos since December, killing at least three soldiers and wounding dozens.

The police say 22 people have been arrested over the incidents but have not released their names. Last month the family of former finance minister Olu Falae said he was being detained over the bombs but said he was innocent.
